claims.text: Disposable income is the income a household has left to spend or to save after taxes on income have been paid, plus any transfer payments such as a pension that it receives.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: A rise in a household's income tends to raise its spending, and higher-income households usually save a larger share of income than lower-income households, so the split between spending and saving differs between households and changes over time as income changes.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: A higher rate of interest raises the reward a household earns on savings deposits and raises the cost of repaying a loan, so households tend to save more and borrow less, and spending on items usually bought on credit tends to fall.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.

claims.text: Confidence influences the split between spending and saving: a household that expects its income to be secure tends to spend more of its income now and to borrow more readily, whereas a household that fears job losses tends to postpone spending and save as a precaution.

verification.method: Authored against the 0455 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft.
